prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor retail aisle where a person in a tan jacket stands in the left foreground roughly 0.5 to 1.0 metres in front of the camera wearer, next to a tiered display counter and wall shelves to the right at 0.6 to 2.0 metres and about 0.3 to 0.5 metres from the person, while an open aisle extends behind them to the left beyond 3 to 5 metres. Both the foreground person and the near edge of the display shelves are within arm's reach of the camera wearer, and the merchandise on the counter and held in the person's hands is within the person's reach. Across the 5 frames, the person shifts from standing very close in frame 1 (~0.5 m) and facing right toward the shelves to stepping slightly back and left (~0.8–1.0 m) while turning toward the camera wearer in frame 4 (with their raised right hand bright white at ~0.5 m) and shifting further left by frame 5 so their lower body and left side are cropped out of the frame. The map clearly separates the foreground person and the hanging garments at the far left edge (~1.0–1.5 m in frames 1–3) from the cluttered background store racks and recessed shelf tiers, which are hard to judge in distance from the busy RGB textures alone. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 1 where the person's torso saturates to uniform white and loses surface contour, and in frame 5 where the person's torso appears abnormally dark (implying a greater distance) compared to their bright foreground hand and the adjacent shelves.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates a single `person` mask in the left-to-center foreground (roughly 0.5 to 1.0 metres from the camera wearer), a purple `book` mask on the lower-right display shelf in frame 3 (~0.8 m away and ~0.2 m in front of the person's hands), and a green `tv` mask on the middle-right shelf in frame 4 (~1.2 m away and ~0.6 m to the person's left). The silhouette contour shows the person facing right in profile in frames 1 to 3 (with the top of their head cropped by the upper frame boundary), turning to face the camera wearer in frame 4, and shifting to the far left edge in frame 5 where their back and lower torso are cut off by the left and bottom borders while their right arm extends right toward the shelves. The person and the nearby display items are within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person, and the person's mask occludes the lower-left aisle and parts of the counter behind them in frames 1 to 3. Compared to the visually cluttered RGB strip, the segmentation map provides a crisp boundary Separating the person's silhouette—including their extended hands in frames 1 and 5—from the densely packed merchandise behind them. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene objects: it fails to segment almost all shelves, racks, and handheld items across the strip, detects the `book` in only one frame, and misclassifies a square framed picture on the shelf in frame 4 as a `tv`.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders yellow body keypoints and a magenta 2D hand skeleton against a black background for the person standing 0.5 to 1.0 metres in front of the camera wearer. In frame 2, the torso and face keypoints show the person in the left-center foreground facing right and angled slightly downward toward the counter, while in frame 4 the symmetric shoulder/hip box, facial cluster, and raised right-hand skeleton at chest height (~0.5 m from the camera) show the person facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer before only their extended right hand remains detected in the lower-left foreground in frame 5 (~0.6 m away). In frames 4 and 5, the magenta hand skeleton makes the exact finger articulation and palm orientation within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the adjacent shelves much easier to see than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it completely misses the person's body and hands in frame 1, misses the left arm and both hands in frame 2, and misses the entire torso and head in frame 5. Most notably, in frame 3 it misses the person entirely and hallucinates an inverted, tilted torso and head skeleton on the lower-right book display (~0.8 m away) where a portrait illustration appears on a book cover.
